newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ING Barings sees Hungary year-end CPI at 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings sees Hungary year-end CPI at 16 pct.

text.p: ING Barings said it was maintaining its inflation forecast for Hungary and said it was neutral over the local fixed income market.

"We maintain our 16 percent year end inflation forecast, based on moderate real wage growth, continued public sector spending cuts and sluggish domestic demand," ING Barings said in the April issue of its "Fixed-income strategy."

Hungary aims to reduce average CPI to around 18 percent in 1997 from 23.6 percent in 1996, while central bank head Gyorgy Suranyi said earlier he expected CPI to fall to 17 percent year-on-year in December.

The Hungarian government is expected to announce an anti-inflation package in May that should include fiscal, monetary and exchange rate policies to bring inflation down to 12 percent by 1998, ING Barings said.
Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told Reuters on Monday that the government was likely to discuss within three weeks two alternative programmes about the reduction of inflation next year.

Medgyessy said the alternative programme, which includes a more radical cut, may push down year-on-year inflation to slightly below 10 percent by December 1998 in the optimal case, pending a price and wage agreement between the government, employers and employees.

He added that year-on-year inflation could go down to between 16 to 17 percent by December 1997 from 18.8 percent in March, adding that he would be able to give a more justified forecast in June, after seeing the May CPI figures.
"In the absence of the implementation of such a package and continued evidence of stronger demand growth, inflation may become more stubborn in 4Q 1997," ING Barings said.
